verdict.justification: Deliverable A is a much cleaner, more accurate, and better-structured SOP than Deliverable B. Deliverable A correctly cites ANSI/ESD S20.20 numerical limits in Section 9 (e.g., footwear system resistance '< 1.0 × 10⁹ Ω' and ionizer offset voltage 'within ± 35 V'), whereas Deliverable B gives an overly restrictive/inaccurate footwear limit ('typically below 35 MΩ', which is the wrist strap limit or the older footwear-only component limit rather than the S20.20 system limit) and omits the ionizer limit. Furthermore, Deliverable B contains internal contradictions and technical errors: in Section 4.2 it says 'Do not touch leads, contacts or component bodies; hold items by the edges or the packaging' (for discrete components, holding the insulated package body while avoiding leads is standard, as A correctly notes in R.3: 'Handle by the package body or board edges'), and in Section 6.1 it permits moving 'open or partly filled containers' outside the EPA if an ESD cart is used, contradicting its own rule in 4.3 that outside the EPA items must be in a closed shielding bag or conductive container. Finally, Deliverable B leaves raw markdown syntax ('**ANSI/ESD S541**') in the Word document and breaks line breaks in its Section 9 table.
